item.title: Batiki families struggle as water sources dry up

item.content:encoded:
Families on Batiki Island in Lomaiviti Province are facing a worsening water shortage, with some households reportedly sharing a single bottle of water among five family members to get through the day. For the people of Batiki, the water crisis is no longer just a concern raised at meetings but a daily struggle affecting their families and communities. Community member Eapi Nabou, from Naigani Village, says the island's four villages and one school are heavily dependent on rainwater harvesting. He says about 90 percent of homes rely on collected rainwater for their daily needs. However, prolonged dry conditions have caused wells and surface water sources on the island to dry up. Nabou says the situation has been particularly difficult over the past five months, with families struggling to access enough water for their basic needs. He says some men have also resorted to bathing in the ocean because of the shortage. Nabou says concerns about water shortages have been raised through traditional channels for more than 20 years, with communities continuing to call for improvements to the island's existing water sources. He says while government assistance has helped with water cartage in recent months, the communities recognise that emergency assistance alone will not solve their long-standing water problems. With the support of their newly registered non-profit organisation, the Lomanitakali Foundation, the community has started exploring solutions and seeking assistance from development partners. Nabou says the community is now exploring more sustainable options, including groundwater extraction and desalination plants. He says the Mineral Resources Department has already conducted a survey and identified potential groundwater sources on the island. However, the community is now seeking government assistance with the machinery and equipment needed to transport a drilling machine to Batiki. This would allow the community to access the identified groundwater sources. Nabou says the community hopes the drilling can be carried out before their remaining water supplies run out, particularly with the expected El Niño peak in January. He says their main concern is ensuring that families back home, particularly children and the elderly, have reliable access to safe drinking water.

item.title: Peni Cabenalevu’s attempted murder case transferred to High Court
item.description: The case of 23-year-old Peni Cabenalevu, who is charged with two counts of assault causing actual bodily harm and two counts of attempted murder, has been transferred to the Suva High Court. Cabenalevu appeared before Magistrate Joseph Daurewa this afternoon, where the prosecution objected to bail. He has been further remanded in custody, and a Domestic Violence Restraining Order (DVRO) has also b
item.content:encoded:
The case of 23-year-old Peni Cabenalevu, who is charged with two counts of assault causing actual bodily harm and two counts of attempted murder, has been transferred to the Suva High Court. Cabenalevu appeared before Magistrate Joseph Daurewa this afternoon, where the prosecution objected to bail. He has been further remanded in custody, and a Domestic Violence Restraining Order (DVRO) has also been issued. It was heard in court that there are four victims, including his wife, in relation to the first assault causing actual bodily harm charge. The matter has been adjourned to 7th December. Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media shows several people running towards a vehicle and attempting to pull the driver out. The driver is then seen attempting to drive away, hitting another vehicle in the process. He is later seen speeding towards the group of men who had tried to pull him out before hitting two police officers. The impact throws both officers into the air. Cabenalevu has also been remanded by Magistrate Yogesh Prasad in relation to another matter involving careless driving. That case has been adjourned to 7th December for his plea.

item.title: All G11 members have applied to contest next general elections under People's Alliance Party - Balawa
item.description: All members of the Group of 11 have applied to contest the next general election under the People's Alliance Party, with their applications currently being processed. The G11 members are Ioane Naivalurua (bloc leader), Viliame Naupoto, Mosese Bulitavu, Naisa Tuinaceva, Josaia Niudamu, Sachida Nand, Shalen Kumar, Aliki Bia, Penioni Ravunawa, Taito Rokomatu and Alipate Tuicolo.
item.content:encoded:
All members of the Group of 11 have applied to contest the next general election under the People's Alliance Party, with their applications currently being processed.

The G11 members are Ioane Naivalurua (bloc leader), Viliame Naupoto, Mosese Bulitavu, Naisa Tuinaceva, Josaia Niudamu, Sachida Nand, Shalen Kumar, Aliki Bia, Penioni Ravunawa, Taito Rokomatu and Alipate Tuicolo.

People's Alliance Party General Secretary Sila Balawa has confirmed to fijivillage News that all G11 members have submitted their applications, which is now going through the party's selection process.

Earlier this morning, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says all applications are first submitted to the General Secretary before being forwarded to the party's Selection Board, followed by the Executive Interview Board, before reaching him.

Meanwhile, the latest election-related opinion polling by the Centre for Democracy and Dialogue, involving 1,673 participants, shows the People's Alliance Party leading with 27.5 percent support.

The survey also found that 13.6 percent of respondents preferred Rabuka as their choice for Prime Minister.

item.title: 23-yr-old man charged with attempted murder following Laucala Bay incident
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/11/2026 A 23-year-old man has been charged and will appear before the Suva Magistrates Court today in relation to an incident in Laucala Bay last Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/11/2026

A 23-year-old man has been charged and will appear before the Suva Magistrates Court today in relation to an incident in Laucala Bay last Thursday.

The man has been charged with two counts of assault causing actual bodily harm and two counts of attempted murder.

A video by Tech360 (Fiji) Limited shows several people running towards a vehicle and trying to pull the driver out.

The driver is then seen attempting to drive away, hitting another vehicle in the process.

The driver is then seen speeding towards the group of men who had tried to pull him out before hitting two police officers.

The impact throws both officers into the air.

item.title: Dry conditions leave fish ponds depleted across the Western Division
item.description: Prolonged dry weather due to El Niño is putting pressure on fish and prawn farmers across the Western Division, with several farms reporting dried-up ponds, droping water levels and reduced production. An El Niño Impact Assessment carried out by the Western Division Aquaculture Team across Nadi District and the provinces of Ba, Ra and Nadroga has identified significant challenges facing aquacultur
item.content:encoded:
Prolonged dry weather due to El Niño is putting pressure on fish and prawn farmers across the Western Division, with several farms reporting dried-up ponds, droping water levels and reduced production.

An El Niño Impact Assessment carried out by the Western Division Aquaculture Team across Nadi District and the provinces of Ba, Ra and Nadroga has identified significant challenges facing aquaculture farmers.

Ministry of Fisheries says in Nadi, falling water levels and pond temperatures reaching 29 degrees Celsius have affected several farms, with some farmers losing their water sources completely.

They say a farm in Tunalia has lost about 100 fish, while some farmers are harvesting early to conserve water and others have switched to borehole water to keep their ponds operating.

They say in Nadroga, nine fish ponds have dried up after their water sources ran dry.

The assessment in Ra covered 30 farms, representing 68 percent of the province's aquaculture farms.

Their findings show that streams, creeks and groundwater levels are falling at 45 percent of the farms assessed, while production has dropped by between 50 and 65 percent on affected farms.

The assessment also identified risks associated with temperature fluctuations, algae blooms and murky water, which could further affect fish health and production.

Immediate needs identified by farmers include fish feed, water pumps and water storage tanks.

The Ministry says farmers have been advised to adjust feeding practices according to changing water levels and temperatures, consider emergency harvesting if their ponds have been stocked for more than three months, and closely monitor their fish for signs of stress.

The Ministry further says it will continue monitoring affected farms and working with farmers on support and adaptation measures as dry conditions persist.

Farmers affected by the conditions are encouraged to contact their nearest Fisheries office.
